draft.definition: Noah, the son whom Lamech names in hope of relief from toil.
draft.evidence: Genesis 5:29 gives the name נֹחַ and explains it through the wordplay on יְנַחֲמֵנוּ, “he will comfort us.”

analysis.evidence: וַיְחִי נֹחַ אַחַר הַמַּבּוּל means “Noah lived after the flood.” The verse names Noah as the man who lived another 350 years.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix. It is the subject of the third-person masculine singular verb וַיְחִי, “he lived.”

analysis.evidence: אַחַר governs הַמַּבּוּל, “the flood.” The phrase locates Noah’s remaining 350 years of life after that event.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew preposition without a prefix or suffix.
